title: Tap-Line Cleaning Interval Tracker
dataSources: Fermentation telemetry (`brew:fermentation`), brew-day records (`brew:batch`), mash probes (`brew:mash`), keg pressure (`kegerator:pressure`), tap pours (`kegerator:pour`), brew-fridge duty logs (`brewfridge:compressor`), cellar climate (`winecellar:reading`), and line-cleaning events (`tapline:clean`).
app: Homebrewing telemetry from Tilt/iSpindel fermentation sensors, Brewfather batch exports, ESPHome mash and fridge probes, keg pressure sensors, tap flow meters, and cellar climate sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=tapline:clean
| stats latest(_time) as last_clean by tap
| eval days_since_clean=round((now()-last_clean)/86400,1)
| sort - days_since_clean
description: Ranks taps by how long it has been since the last documented line cleaning.
value: Line cleaning is easy to postpone and directly affects beer quality, so a simple aging report helps keep keg service disciplined.
implementation: Log each tap-line cleaning event from a checklist app, NFC tag, or Home Assistant button press.
visualization: Bar chart of days since last cleaning per tap.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces which beer lines have gone the longest without a clean, so your pours stay fresher and safer.
